Project an sf object to a CRS suited to its extent

Source: R/crs-geometry.R
ensure_projected.Rd

Returns a spatial object in a projected CRS, so that distances and areas computed on it are close to true. Without target_crs, an object that already has a projected CRS is returned as it is, and lon/lat input is moved to a CRS chosen from its extent; with target_crs, the object is moved to that CRS.

Usage

ensure_projected(x, target_crs = NULL, purpose = c("distance", "area"))

Arguments

x

An sf or sfc object (other objects are returned unchanged).

target_crs

Optional target CRS (sf object, integer EPSG, or crs). Must resolve to a usable CRS via sf::st_crs(); an unusable value (one that resolves to NA_crs_) raises an error, so x is never left unprojected without a word.

purpose

"distance" (default): the candidate that distorts pairwise distances least, which is what ranges, block sizes, bandwidths and length-scales read off the coordinates. "area": an equal-area projection, for densities or rates per cell. For lon/lat input the choice is then made among a Lambert azimuthal centred on the data and an Albers conic (where its parallels do not degenerate or pass a pole), whichever distorts distances less; a UTM zone, which is not equal-area, never enters that comparison, and global coverage gets Equal Earth in place of Web Mercator. For input already projected, the area distortion is measured and a warning is logged above 1 percent; see "Equal-area check". Ignored when target_crs is given.

Value

x in target_crs when one is given. Otherwise x in the projected CRS chosen here, as it came when it already had a projected CRS, or without a CRS when it had none and the lon/lat test declined it (see "Missing CRS"). Two attributes record how the CRS was reached:

crs_choice

Present when a projection was chosen here (lon/lat input, no target_crs): a data.frame with one row per projection considered, holding name, crs (its definition), the measured worst-case distance_error (relative, over sampled pairs; NA where it could not be measured) and chosen. The figure is measured for the single candidate on the paths where no comparison runs (a UTM zone on a local extent, the equal-area projection chosen for a layer straddling the antimeridian). NULL when no local projection was chosen here: input that already had a projected CRS, a target_crs you supplied, or an extent no local projection fits, which falls back to Web Mercator or Equal Earth.

crs_assumed

On input without a CRS: "EPSG:4326" when the lon/lat test took the coordinates for degrees, "none" when it declined. The attribute is also read on the way in: an object already carrying "none" is returned as it is, without the test, which is how a predict() method replays a fit's decision so that a subset of the training rows is not judged differently from the whole.

Details

Without target_crs, only geographic (lon/lat) input is transformed, and the CRS chosen depends on the extent of the data:

Local extents

The UTM zone containing the data's centre (EPSG:326xx north of the equator, EPSG:327xx south). Distances and areas are close to true over a few degrees of longitude, which is the case this package is usually in. The centre is the centroid on the sphere, computed with s2 whatever sf::sf_use_s2() is set to, so data near a zone edge get the same zone in every session.

Wide extents

Once the data reach well beyond the roughly 3 degrees a UTM zone is designed for, a single zone can distort distances by several percent, and that error propagates into variogram ranges, block sizes, GWR bandwidths and GP length-scales. The projection used is then the one with the smallest measured distortion among the zone, a Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on the data and (where its standard parallels do not degenerate or pass a pole) an Albers conic. Each is scored by projecting representative points of the data and comparing planar with geodesic distances over the pairs at least 1 mm apart. A non-POINT layer is reduced to one point per feature, plus the vertices of its outline when fewer than 40 distinct points remain, so a single study-area polygon is scored too, however many rows repeat it; copies of one location count once, and rows without a finite location are left out. A candidate must place every location of the layer to be used: one under which a vertex of the layer has no coordinates (a UTM zone about 90 degrees or more from its central meridian) gets distance_error NA and is not chosen, and the log line names it. A vertex at a latitude beyond 90, which no CRS places, takes no part in this test. When no candidate places every vertex, Web Mercator (Equal Earth for purpose = "area") is used. The choice, its distance error and the zone's, and this argument are logged (see spatialkit_quiet()); they are not R warnings, so tryCatch(warning = ) does not see them.

Antimeridian

Data straddling longitude 180 have a bounding box wider than a hemisphere. The wrap is detected from the coordinates (one very large gap in the sorted longitudes) and an equal-area projection centred on the true extent is used.

Around a pole

Data spanning more than 180 degrees of longitude with no such gap surround a pole. When every point also lies on one side of the equator (Antarctic stations, a pan-Arctic network), a Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on that pole is used, provided it measures a smaller distance error than the global fallback. Web Mercator splits such a layer at longitude 180 and stretches it towards the pole. Only the coverage left over, spanning both hemispheres or a low-latitude belt the polar projection fits worse, falls back to EPSG:3857 (Equal Earth for purpose = "area").

Missing CRS

A layer without a CRS is read by the lon/lat test of spatialkit-geometry ("Layers without a CRS"). With no target_crs, coordinates the test takes for degrees are read as EPSG:4326, with a warning, and the rules above then apply; coordinates it declines are left as they are. With target_crs, coordinates the test takes for degrees are read as EPSG:4326 and reprojected to the target, with a warning, and any others have the target stamped on without reprojection. A stamp is a relabel, logged only, so check that the coordinates are in that CRS. Set the CRS on x to avoid either. A target_crs in longitude and latitude is not stamped on coordinates that cannot be in it: an x outside -180 to 360 or a y beyond 90 north or south, in the box of the coordinates that have a location, stops the call with an error that gives the box.

Rows without a location

Such rows (see spatialkit-geometry, "Rows without a location") take no part in the lon/lat test or the choice of a projection. The lon/lat test reads the coordinates that have a location vertex by vertex, so a polygon with one vertex beyond 1e150 is read on its other vertices. A layer in which no row has a location, or each row of which is empty, has no location or has a vertex at a latitude beyond 90, gets Web Mercator (Equal Earth for purpose = "area"). Moved to another CRS, a row without a location comes back empty, in its own geometry type. A row that has a location and that the move cannot place in full comes back empty, or without the vertices the CRS cannot place, with a warning of class spatialkit_rows_unplaced that names the rows (rows on the condition). With the projection chosen here that happens only at a coordinate no CRS places, such as a latitude beyond 90; with a target_crs, wherever that CRS cannot place the layer.

target_crs overrides all of this. Pass it whenever you need a specific, reproducible projection: comparing runs, matching an existing layer, or fixing the units that make_folds()'s block_size will be interpreted in.

A layer that mixes XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries is returned in XY when it is transformed, with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped, and the projection is chosen from the layer in XY; see spatialkit-geometry, "Mixed dimensions, Z and M". A layer that is not transformed is returned with its own geometry.

Equal-area check

Under purpose = "area", input that already has a projected CRS is returned as it is, but its area distortion over the extent is measured and logged as a warning when it exceeds 1 percent. The measure is the spread of planar-to-geodesic area ratios over probe polygons. The probes are the layer's distinct polygons (exact copies of a polygon count once). A 6 by 6 grid over the bounding box is used instead for a layer without polygons, a layer of one distinct polygon, which gives one ratio and no spread, and a layer with a polygon s2 cannot measure in degrees (edges that cross, a spike) or that sf::st_is_valid() rejects in its CRS (a hole outside its shell), whose planar area is not the area it encloses. When the grid gives no figure either (a single point, a line along one axis), a warning says that the distortion could not be measured. An equal-area projection still shows some spread, from the sphere the geodesic areas are computed on against the ellipsoid the projection uses. summarize_by_cell() applies the same check before it computes a density.

See also

spatialkit-geometry for how input geometry and CRSs are read.

Other data preparation: [.spatialkit_rows(), coerce_to_points(), harmonize_crs(), prep_model_data(), spatialkit-geometry

Examples

library(sf)
pts_ll <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(lon = c(9.1, 9.2), lat = c(48.7, 48.8)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326
)
# A local extent gets the containing UTM zone; the zone's measured
# distance error over the extent travels with the result.
st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll))$epsg  # 32632
#> [1] 32632
attr(ensure_projected(pts_ll), "crs_choice")
#>          name        crs distance_error chosen
#> 1 UTM zone 32 EPSG:32632   0.0003984524   TRUE

# A continental extent is scored against the zone and may get an
# equal-area projection instead.  The choice is logged with its distance
# error and the zone's, not raised as an R warning (see ?spatialkit_quiet);
# crs_choice holds every candidate scored.
wide <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(lon = c(-120, -70), lat = c(30, 48)),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326
)
wide_p <- ensure_projected(wide)
st_crs(wide_p)$proj4string
#> [1] "+proj=aea +lat_0=41.729902 +lon_0=-98.42263 +lat_1=33 +lat_2=45 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
attr(wide_p, "crs_choice")[, c("name", "distance_error", "chosen")]
#>                                                      name distance_error chosen
#> 1                                             UTM zone 14   0.0175763956  FALSE
#> 2   Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on (-98.4, 41.7)   0.0055662736  FALSE
#> 3 Albers equal-area (lat_1=33.0, lat_2=45.0, lon_0=-98.4)   0.0001446928   TRUE

# target_crs overrides the choice.
st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll, target_crs = 3035))$epsg  # 3035
#> [1] 3035

# For densities per cell the CRS has to be equal-area.  Two candidates are
# scored, an Albers conic and a Lambert azimuthal, both centred on the data,
# and whichever distorts distance less over the extent is used: here Albers.
st_crs(ensure_projected(pts_ll, purpose = "area"))$proj4string
#> [1] "+proj=aea +lat_0=48.750011 +lon_0=9.14995 +lat_1=48.716667 +lat_2=48.783333 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
